engagement_title: Sable & Finch Realty coastal listing tour: cut a wandering handheld walkthrough into a calm tour with a clean voice, bring the dusk exteriors to one evening look for the cover, build editable listing captions, and print the open-house card for all twelve active listings
vertical: Real Estate, Construction and Property. A four agent residential team on the North Shore of Massachusetts, listing a 1930s shingled single family house in Marblehead at just over 1.2 million dollars.
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post 'Real Estate Listing / Property Tour Video Editor' quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, in which a realtor supplies raw handheld property walkthrough clips plus a few exterior shots and asks for a polished branded listing tour: trim and sequence the best shots into a sizzle, add branded lower thirds carrying the address, the price and the agent, an intro title and an end card, one consistent colour grade, exported for MLS and the listing website plus a vertical social cut and a thumbnail. The real post names no company, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Sable and Finch Realty and the agents stay unnamed. REASONABLY ENRICHED into the fuller commission that client actually needed rather than the video edit alone: the same team prints an open house card for every active listing, so the engagement carries the card run as a genuine record per page variable data job off their own existing printed card, and the captions are delivered as something the team can retype next week rather than baked pixels, because the post's own reason for hiring (four or five listings a month, prices move) makes editability the whole point. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest: a real press PDF converts into a live merge template headlessly, and HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes.
client_one_liner: Our junior agent filmed the whole house and it wanders, our listing agent recorded her voice in the car, our favourite dusk exteriors have no sky left in them, and the open house is in nine days.
client_brief:
Sable and Finch Realty, coastal listing tour

We list on the North Shore of Massachusetts. The new one is a 1930s shingled house two streets back from the water in Marblehead, asking just over one point two million, and it goes live in nine days.

What we have. Our junior agent walked the house with a gimbal and filmed every room plus two passes outside. It is long, it wanders, and there is a stretch where he talks to the homeowner's dog. We also have the exterior stills our photographer took at dusk, and a voice track our listing agent recorded reading the highlights.

What we need. A tour video for the listing page and the MLS, cut down to the parts that sell the house, with her voice over it sounding like she is in a room and not in a car. A tall version of the same tour for social. One still for the cover and the listing thumbnail, and it should be an evening shot, because that is what makes people click on a house like this. Captions that sit over the footage carrying the address, the price, the bed and bath count and the school district, and we need those as something we can edit ourselves, because the price will move and we run four or five of these a month.

We also print a card for the open house. Our card from last year is attached as a PDF. We want the same card, one page per property, for all twelve of our current listings, and it has to be right on every one of them, not only on the first one we look at.

Buyers for this house are moving up, mostly families in their late thirties, and they are choosing between this and three others. It should feel calm and warm and unhurried. Loud, saturated and fast makes it look like a cheaper house.

And a note on what you did, what type we are on, and anything we should know.
price_band_and_audience: A 1.2 million dollar coastal single family listing sold to move up buyers aged roughly 35 to 48 with children, choosing between three or four comparable houses in the same school district. The band is load bearing. At this price the tour has to be slow, warm and near neutral, with long held frames, restrained captioning and an evening cover: the buyer is reassuring herself about a large decision, and calm reads as confidence. Push the same material into a saturated, fast cut, caption heavy treatment with hard cuts on every beat and it reads as a 400,000 dollar starter home listing and the move up buyer stops watching, which is the exact failure the team is paying to avoid. Push the other way into a near silent, near black, no text luxury film and it misprices the house upward and confuses buyers who genuinely need the bed count and the school district on screen. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Residential real estate: a boutique agent team listing coastal single family homes on Massachusetts' North Shore.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Marblehead, Massachusetts, a four agent residential team running four or five listings a month.
brand_identity.about: Sable and Finch Realty sells character homes along the North Shore to move up families who are choosing carefully between a small number of houses. We present a property the way a buyer wants to feel about it: calm, warm and reassuring. Our work is quiet on purpose, because at this price calm reads as confidence.
brand_identity.audience: Move up buyers roughly 35 to 48 with children, weighing this house against three or four comparable homes in the same school district, who need the facts on screen and the feeling in the frame.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Homes around and above 1.2 million dollars, the established coastal middle of the market. Presentation sits between a fast starter home listing and a near silent luxury film, and must read as neither.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, warm text serif for names and headings paired with a restrained sans for facts and captions. Type stays small and calm: address, price, beds and baths and school district carried plainly, never loud, never dense. Evening warmth over crisp cool.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, measured, reassuring, never a hard sell. Example: "Two streets back from the water, shingled, and the porch light is already on."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no packaged brand kit. Last season's open house card survives only as the printer's press PDF, and the on screen captions have always been rebuilt by hand each listing. Colour and type live in prior collateral rather than in a guideline anyone can hand over.
brand_identity.values: Honest presentation of a real property. Every figure a buyer relies on, the price, the bed and bath count, the school district and the disclosure line, must be exactly right on every piece.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_walkthrough_raw/ (7 clips, 16:9)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld gimbal walkthrough filmed by a junior agent in one visit, room by room, plus two exterior passes.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole house plus two passes outside. It wanders and there is a stretch where he talks to the dog."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the seven clips were filmed on a phone at a much lower capture size after the gimbal battery died, and those two carry the only footage of the kitchen and the back stair. Because re aspecting and resizing never add pixels and the highlight cut only shortens what it is given, any master that includes those rooms is ceilinged by them rather than by the five good clips, and the vertical cut is ceilinged harder still. One exterior pass was also held portrait, so it cannot be widened into the landscape master at all. Nothing in the filenames or the client's description separates the two capture generations.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_exteriors/ (11 stills, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Dusk exterior stills of the house shot by the team's photographer across about twenty minutes of falling light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The dusk exteriors. Our favourite is the one with the porch lights on."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two frames the team likes best were exposed for the lit porch interior, so the sky across the upper third is clipped flat and a highlight recovery move on those frames returns a result in which nothing visibly changes. Separately one of the two is about two and a half degrees off level, and levelling it eats exactly the roofline that the cover crop needs to keep, so straightening and cropping cannot both be satisfied on that frame.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_agent_vo.wav
assets_supplied.kind: Voice track of the listing agent reading the highlights, recorded on a phone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Her read of the highlights. She did it in the car between showings."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The last portion is a second take recorded at a noticeably different distance from the phone and at a slower pace than the first, and there is a steady blower hum underneath the whole thing. Speech enhancement evens the tone and lifts the voice out of the hum, but it does not make the two takes the same read, so any cut timed against the first take drifts against the second.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_open_house_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The team's existing printed open house card from last season, supplied as the template for the run.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's card. We want the same card for every listing."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Printed, the card shows four clearly separated blocks. Its text was actually set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes far coarser frame granularity than the printed page suggests. Worse, the mapping readout omits one run from the middle of that story while keeping its line break, so the readout still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly the length of the dropped run. The validator returns valid on those offsets and the placeholder step reports success, and the fields past the omission simply never land.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_listings.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve active listings: address, town, price, beds, baths, square feet, school district, open house window, agent line.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All twelve of our current listings. The open house times are already correct."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the twelve addresses are long enough that at trim they run past the card's fixed measure. A fixed text frame does not spill and does not flag: it simply stops rendering, so those records come out truncated in the middle of a street name while the merge reports success and the page count is exactly right. One further row carries a price with a range rather than a single figure, which reads as an error on a printed card.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_look_reference.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A warm still the team pulled from a tour video by another firm that they admire, supplied purely as a look reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the feeling we want. Warm, slow, not shiny."

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_facts_and_disclosure.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the listing facts for the featured house, the caption copy, and the brokerage disclosure line that must appear on every printed card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The facts and the disclosure. The disclosure wording cannot be changed."

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_mark_scan.png
assets_supplied.kind: The Sable and Finch lockup, a small finch perched on a branch emblem beside the SABLE AND FINCH wordmark, the only surviving copy, exported small from the team's old email signature.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our little finch logo. We only have this one small copy of it, off an old email footer."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a low resolution raster with soft anti aliased edges and a faint halo, and the mark is Finch Gold sitting on a Shell ground at low contrast. A default trace reads the halo as edge and returns a furry multi node outline, and at that low contrast a luminance or ink level selection closes the finch's eye counter and merges the fine branch strokes. Nothing shows at screen size: the trace looks clean until it is placed at the card's roughly fourteen millimetre lockup and the end card size, where the eye fills in and the branch gaps close. The mark has to be selected by its own gold hue and thresholded to a clean bi level before the trace, and confirmed at reproduction size rather than on screen.

acceptance_bar: The tour reads as one calm evening piece: one warm target across every graded frame, one pace, and no moment where the picture visibly changes generation mid sequence.

No delivered video or still exceeds the pixel dimensions of the material it was made from, and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. A cover that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The vertical cut is genuinely derived from the master rather than being a separately reasoned edit, and its size ceiling is stated honestly rather than asserted.
The voice sounds like one person in one room across the whole tour. If the second take cannot be brought to the first, it is named in the note rather than shipped hoping nobody hears it.
The cover still is an evening frame with sky that still has something in it. A frame whose sky cannot be brought back is not delivered flat and called moody.
The captions are live editable text in a working file the team can retype, not a picture of a caption, and they stay readable over the brightest part of the footage they sit on.
All three caption canvases are in one working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the self contained source it was built from is delivered alongside.
The open house run is one page per listing for all twelve, and every page is correct: every field present, nothing truncated at the measure, and the disclosure line on all of them.
No listing card silently drops a field. A template that reports success while a field never landed fails, whether or not anyone noticed on page one.
One type system across the captions and the cards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The note states, per photograph and per clip, what was applied and why, every resize any tool reported, which rooms are ceilinged by the phone footage, and what could not be delivered.

The capture generation split is established by reading each clip's true dimensions rather than by its filename, and the master and vertical ceilings follow from that reading: the phone generation rooms and the portrait pass are named as ceilings, not discovered by a viewer later.

The Sable and Finch mark on the cards, the end card and the captions is recovered vector artwork rather than a re embedded raster, and the finch's eye counter and the branch gaps stay open at the card's lockup size instead of filling in.

adobe_surfaces.tools: video_metadata (reading each clip's true capture dimensions), media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize
adobe_surfaces.role: The tour itself. Before any of that, video_metadata reads each clip's true capture dimensions, which is the only thing that separates the two capture generations and the portrait pass the filenames hide, and it is the synchronous read the motion ceiling is verified against. Summarisation is how the agent finds which minutes of a wandering walkthrough are worth keeping without watching the whole thing blind, speech enhancement lifts the voice out of the car and its blower, the highlight cut shortens the assembled walkthrough into the tour (it only ever shortens, so nothing can be lengthened back), and the re aspect produces the vertical from the master without ever adding a pixel, which is what makes the phone footage ceiling a real constraint rather than a preference.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked, and thresholding the mark to bi level before the trace), image_adjust_highlights, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox, and selecting the mark by its own gold hue), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize (recovering the brand mark to clean paths)
adobe_surfaces.role: Everything still. It levels what is off level before any crop is chosen, sets one warm evening target and brings each dusk exterior toward it one call at a time, confines corrections to the lit porch or to the sky where a whole frame move would take the shingles orange, cuts the cover and thumbnail without ever enlarging, and reads what each call actually reported rather than that it succeeded. It also recovers the Sable and Finch mark from its only surviving low resolution scan, selecting the mark by its own gold hue and thresholding it to a clean bi level before the vector trace so the finch's eye counter and branch gaps survive at the card's lockup size rather than filling in.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The caption set and the end card as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a referenced photograph renders as an empty grey box at full success, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels as an uploaded file because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (including its validator mode), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The open house run off the team's own printed card, one record per page for all twelve listings, plus the press PDF and the proof raster. This surface is where the offsets have to be computed from the document's true story text rather than from the readout, where the placeholders have to be verified by round tripping the document rather than by believing the success message, and where a fixed measure decides whether a long address survives to trim.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system carrying the on screen captions and the printed cards. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land calm and warm rather than corporate or luxury. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name has to be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back with no warning.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the team does not own, a New England coastal town streetscape for the card's neighbourhood panel, IP clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative results excluded. The Boards half persists the selects the four agents sign off from inside the nine day window, placed within the per call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and decide which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The captions must be editable next week, which puts them on the authoring surface rather than into the video; the card run is one record per page at volume, which is the one thing the merge surface is actually for. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export later.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but the manifest has to carry each clip's capture size beside its role, because that is the number the whole motion half is later bounded by.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role, with capture sizes recorded.

trajectory.action: Read video_metadata on every one of the seven clips first, because the filenames and the client's one shoot description do not separate the capture generations, then look at all seven clips and all eleven exteriors: which clips are the gimbal generation and which are the phone generation, which is the portrait pass that can never widen into the landscape master, which rooms exist only on the phone clips, which exterior is off level, and which dusk frames have a sky.
trajectory.judgement: The team describes one shoot. Two capture generations and a portrait pass inside one walkthrough is the sort of thing only the material reveals when its true dimensions are read, not something a filename or a preview thumbnail shows, and it decides both what the tour can contain and what the vertical can be.
trajectory.produces: A per clip and per frame triage note covering capture size read from video_metadata, orientation, illuminant, tilt and which rooms are ceilinged.

trajectory.action: Summarise the walkthrough clips to find the beats that sell the house rather than watching for the parts to remove.
trajectory.judgement: A wandering forty minute walkthrough has maybe four minutes in it. Choosing by what the buyer needs to see, the water side windows, the kitchen, the stair, the porch at dusk, is art direction, and the dog stretch is not the only thing that should go.
trajectory.produces: A beat list naming the keeps and the reason each earns its place.

trajectory.action: Enhance the voice track, then listen to the whole of it rather than the opening.
trajectory.judgement: Enhancement fixes the room and the hum. It does not reconcile two takes recorded at different distances and different paces, and the second take is where the timing will fight the picture.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned voice track and a written note on where the read changes.

trajectory.action: Cut the master tour to the beat list, pacing it slow and holding frames rather than cutting on every move.
trajectory.judgement: The cut is where the price band becomes visible. This buyer is reassuring herself, so long held frames and few cuts, and the phone generation rooms placed where the change of picture is least conspicuous.
trajectory.produces: The landscape master tour with a written cut rationale.

trajectory.action: Derive the vertical cut from the master and state its honest ceiling.
trajectory.judgement: Re aspecting never adds pixels, so the vertical is bounded by the smallest clip that survives into it, and the portrait exterior pass cannot join the landscape master at all. The choice is whether to keep a ceilinged room or lose it from the vertical.
trajectory.produces: The vertical tour plus a written statement of what bounded it.

trajectory.action: Level the exteriors that are off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Levelling reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and on one frame it takes the roofline the cover wants.
trajectory.produces: Levelled exterior masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one warm evening target from the strongest dusk frame, bring each exterior toward it with its own call, and pull the highlights back on the frames the team likes best.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eleven good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set across frames shot twenty minutes apart under falling light, which is exactly wrong here.
trajectory.produces: Graded exteriors at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine the corrections that a whole frame move gets wrong, selecting the material by its own visual properties rather than by the thing it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Naming the house pulls the selection to the building; the lit porch and the shingle field need separate treatment or the warmth that saves the sky turns the shingles orange.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have broken one half to fix the other.

trajectory.action: Cut the cover still and the thumbnail from the chosen exterior, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The cover carries the click. Optical framing on a house is not geometric centring, and the crop tool will interpolate up to a hard cap while saying so only inside its own tradeoffs.
trajectory.produces: The cover still and the thumbnail with their tradeoff records transcribed.

trajectory.action: Recover the Sable and Finch mark from its only surviving low resolution scan: select the mark by its own gold hue rather than by luminance, threshold it to a clean bi level, run image_vectorize, and render the result at the card's roughly fourteen millimetre lockup size and the end card size to see whether the finch's eye counter and the branch gaps hold.
trajectory.judgement: The scan is Finch Gold on a Shell ground at low contrast with a soft anti aliased halo. A default trace reads the halo as edge and closes the fine detail, and none of it shows at screen size, so the only honest test is the mark at reproduction size, not the trace's success message.
trajectory.produces: The recovered mark as clean vector artwork with a note on what the raw scan could not give, ready to place as the static lockup on the card, the end card and the captions.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the coastal town streetscape, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the evening target, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a calm 1.2 million dollar move up listing rather than a luxury tower or a starter home. A weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the lower third caption, the square cross post frame and the end card at three canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, inline the recovered vector mark on the end card and the caption roots as vector rather than letting it fall back to a raster, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A referenced photograph is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how little the caption can say and still carry the address, the price, the beds and baths and the school district.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole caption set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for canvases two and three.
trajectory.judgement: Every normalisation this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Convert the open house card PDF, export the document structure, ask for the mapping readout, then reconstruct the true story text from the exported document itself and compute every offset from that string.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows four blocks; what the conversion exposes is whatever it exposes, and the readout of a story is not the story. The only defensible source of an offset is the document's own reconstructed text.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory, the true story text, a mapping built on offsets computed from it, and the recovered vector mark placed as the static lockup art on the template so it prints identically on every record.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then round trip the prepared document and confirm every expected field is actually present before any record is merged.
trajectory.judgement: The placeholder step reports success while silently dropping mappings, and the validator returns valid on offsets that are wrong. Verification has to read the document, not the response.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template with every field confirmed present, or a named list of the ones that did not land.

trajectory.action: Merge all twelve listings one record per page, proof every page rather than the first, render the press PDF and the proof raster, then create the selects board and write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: A fixed measure does not spill, it stops, so a long address truncates while the page count stays exactly right. Proofing page one and counting pages is the failure mode. A partial board response is partial, and only the entries it names as failed are re sent.
trajectory.produces: A twelve page press PDF, per record proofs, a persistent selects board, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the one walkthrough is actually two capture generations plus a portrait pass, and where the ceiling sits. Reading video_metadata on the seven clips returns their true dimensions: two clips come back at 1280 by 720, and those two carry the only footage of the kitchen and the back stair, so any master or vertical that keeps those rooms is bounded by 720 lines and not by the five 4K clips; one exterior pass comes back 2160 by 3840 portrait, so it can never widen into the 16:9 landscape master at all. None of this is in the filenames, the client describes one shoot, and the clips read as one walkthrough in a preview until their dimensions are read.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: the true capture size is a property of each file that only video_metadata reports, and the defensible order already reads it during triage before any cut is planned. (b) Nothing states it: the brief describes a single gimbal walkthrough and names no resolutions, and the acceptance line about not exceeding source pixels is the standing constraint, not a disclosure of which clips are small. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response re plans the cut, deciding whether the kitchen and back stair are kept at their real ceiling or lost, where the phone generation is least conspicuous, and what the vertical can honestly contain once the portrait pass is understood to be unusable in the landscape master.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the master around the true ceilings rather than the filenames, place or drop the two phone generation rooms deliberately, re derive the vertical from the master with its ceiling stated honestly, and record each clip's read dimensions in the manifest so the delivered files can be checked against their real sources.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A landscape master or a vertical cut delivered above the pixels the phone footage actually holds, upscaled in all but name, or a portrait pass stretched into the wide frame, shipped as if the whole shoot were one clean 4K capture.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two dusk exteriors the team likes best have any sky left to recover. Both frames were exposed for the lit porch interior, and the only way to learn what remains above the roofline is to pull the highlights and look at the result, where the readout is that nothing visibly moves: the tool reports a successful adjustment and returns a frame that is indistinguishable from the one that went in. Which of the eleven frames this is true of is a property of each individual exposure, and the frames read the same in a preview grid because a clipped sky and a bright sky look alike until something is asked of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: recovery has to be attempted on a real frame to learn whether there is anything under the clip, and the defensible order already puts levelling and grading before the crop is chosen. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the exteriors were shot at dusk and names a favourite, and the acceptance line about an evening cover with something in the sky is the client's standing art direction, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is to move the cover to a different exterior entirely, which changes the crop, the grade target the rest of the set is brought to, and what the end card type has to sit on.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re judge the cover candidate across the whole exterior set rather than the two the team named, re fix the evening target off whichever frame actually holds, bring the remaining exteriors to that revised target, re cut the cover and the thumbnail from the new frame, and tell the team plainly why their favourite is not the cover.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A listing cover whose upper third is flat paper white where an evening sky should be, delivered as the single image that decides whether a move up buyer clicks on a 1.2 million dollar house.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark holds at the size it is actually printed and shown. The only surviving copy of the Sable and Finch mark is a low resolution scan of Finch Gold on a Shell ground at low contrast with a soft anti aliased halo. A default trace looks clean at screen size, but only rendering the vector at the card's roughly fourteen millimetre lockup and the end card size reveals that the halo was traced as a furry multi node outline and that the low contrast closed the finch's eye counter and merged the fine branch strokes. The trace reports success and looks right in a large preview, so nothing but the reproduction size view exposes it, and the same failure recurs if the mark drops to a raster on the Express import, visible only in the returned per canvas markup.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the vectoriser trace succeeds and previews clean regardless, and the halo and the closed counter only appear at reproduction size, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief supplies the mark as the logo and asks for the same card, saying nothing about its resolution or contrast. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is to select the mark by its own gold hue rather than by luminance, threshold it to a clean bi level, and re trace, then to re place and re confirm it at reproduction size on the card, the end card and the captions.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re select the mark by hue, threshold to bi level, re vectorise, render again at the card lockup and end card size to confirm the eye counter and branch gaps are open, and re place the corrected vector on all three surfaces, confirming on the Express import that it stayed vector rather than falling back to a raster.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A brand mark that looks fine on screen but prints as a furry gold blob with a filled in eye on twelve open house cards and sits re rasterised on the end card and the captions the team will reuse four or five times a month.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construction the captions depend on for legibility. A caption sitting over moving footage is built the obvious way as a softly blurred scrim behind the text with layered shadow under the type, and the importer discards a blur outright and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, both at full success with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports what survived, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the square cross post frame and the end card can be checked no other way. Whether the address and price still read against the brightest part of the footage, or sit on a hard edged grey slab, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of that surface, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible legibility constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only that the captions stay readable over the footage. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different construction, a gradient panel or a solid house scrim baked as part of the authored art, and the caption then has to be re composed around whichever one holds.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the legibility as a construct the importer keeps, re author all three canvases around it, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An editable caption file in which the price and the address are unreadable over the bright water side windows on the two canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout, handed to a team who will now put it on screen four or five times a month.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printed open house card actually is once it is converted, and whether the mapping the readout supports is the mapping that lands. The card prints as four separate blocks, but the frame granularity a conversion exposes is not under anyone's control and can be far coarser than the printed page suggests. On top of that the mapping readout omits one run from the middle of the story while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly the dropped run's length, the validator returns valid on those wrong offsets with no warning, and the placeholder step reports completed successfully while the fields past the omission never land at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the readout is the only thing any tool offers before preparing, and both the validator and the prepare step affirm the wrong mapping. A careful agent cannot do it right first time because doing it right requires already distrusting a readout that reports success and a validator that reports valid. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that they want the same card for every listing. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is to build the offsets from a different source entirely, the document's own reconstructed story text, and to change the verification method from reading responses to reading the document.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the exported document, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping, prepare again, round trip the prepared document and confirm each expected field is genuinely present, and only then merge and proof all twelve pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve printed open house cards that pass a page count check and look right on page one while two fields, plausibly the price and the open house window, are silently missing from every card in the run, printed and put out on twelve properties.

deliverables.name: Sable and Finch listing tour, landscape master and vertical cut
deliverables.spec: One calm landscape tour for the listing page and the MLS, cut from the walkthrough to the beats that sell the house, carrying the enhanced voice read as one voice in one room, plus a vertical cut derived from that master rather than reasoned separately. Neither output exceeds the pixel dimensions of the material it was made from, and the honest ceiling imposed by the phone generation clips is stated rather than hidden.

deliverables.name: Sable and Finch evening exterior set and listing cover
deliverables.spec: The dusk exteriors brought to one warm evening target (one white point, one black point, one treatment of the lit porch against the sky), plus one licensed camera scale streetscape frame graded into the same world, and from that set the cover still and the listing thumbnail cut without enlargement. Per frame parameter log, including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours and which frames could not be brought.

deliverables.name: Listing caption set and end card, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes: the lower third caption for the landscape tour, the square cross post frame, and the end card. Live editable text in one licensed type system, every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and legibility over the footage achieved by a construction that actually survives the import on all three canvases. Delivered with the self contained source, which is the durable half: the team edits the document next week and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Open house card run, twelve listings
deliverables.spec: One press PDF at one page per listing for all twelve active listings, derived from the team's own printed card, with every mapped field verified present in the template before the merge and every page proofed after it. No record truncated at the measure, the brokerage disclosure line on every page, plus per record proofs for the four agents to check their own listings and a 300 dpi proof raster.

deliverables.name: Sable and Finch mark, recovered as vector artwork
deliverables.spec: The brand's finch and branch lockup recovered from its only surviving low resolution scan via image_vectorize, cleaned so the finch's eye counter and the branch gaps stay open at the card's roughly fourteen millimetre lockup size and the video end card size, delivered as scalable vector artwork in Finch Gold and placed as the static lockup on the twelve card merge template, on the end card and beside the captions. Recovered by selecting the mark by its own gold hue and thresholding to a clean bi level before the trace, confirmed to survive at reproduction size and to stay vector rather than a re embedded raster through the Express import, with a note on what the raw scan could not give.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per clip and per photograph what was applied and why, the capture generation split and exactly which rooms are ceilinged by it, the state of the second voice take, every resize any tool reported, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, and anything the team should know before running the next listing themselves. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion, which are still, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and only one is genuinely editable next week.
Which minutes of a wandering walkthrough sell this specific house to this specific buyer, which is art direction and not a de duplication exercise.
How to place the phone generation rooms in the cut so the change of picture is least conspicuous, or whether to lose a room rather than show it.
What the vertical cut can honestly contain once re aspecting is understood to never add pixels, and how to say so to a client who assumes a tall version is free.
Whether the second voice take can be brought to the first, or whether it has to be named as a limitation rather than shipped.
Which exterior carries the cover, judged on what survives a recovery attempt rather than on which frame the team named as their favourite.
On the one frame where levelling eats the roofline the cover wants, whether to level and lose the roofline, or crop level and keep it, or move the cover elsewhere.
How little a caption can say and still carry the address, the price, the bed and bath count and the school district at this price band, where density itself reads downmarket.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a calm coastal move up listing, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the mapping is built on the readout or on the document's own reconstructed text, and what verification counts as verification once success messages are known to be unreliable.
Whether a licensed streetscape frame joins the world the graded exteriors live in or reads plainly as bought.

Which clips are the gimbal generation, which are the phone generation and which is the portrait pass, resolved by reading each clip's true dimensions rather than trusting the filename or the one shoot description, and what ceiling that imposes on the master and the vertical.

Whether the recovered mark holds the finch's eye counter and the branch gaps at the card's lockup size and the end card size, or whether the low resolution anti aliased scan forces selecting the mark by its own gold hue and thresholding to bi level before the trace, and re cutting it if it fills in once placed.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image or video model and it returns a nice looking house film about no particular house. IDENTITY: this is one actual property with its actual rooms, its actual porch at its actual dusk, and one actual agent's voice reading approved copy; a regenerated interior is a different house and puts the brokerage in breach of the listing. SPEC: twelve open house cards, one page per listing, every field from the roster present and untruncated with a disclosure line whose wording cannot change, and a cover and thumbnail at exact sizes with no interpolated pixels, none of which a generated image satisfies or can even be checked for. EDITABILITY: the captions are defined by being editable, since the price moves and the team runs four or five of these a month and explicitly cannot re commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this sky have anything under the clip, did this legibility construction survive the import, did this field actually land in the template, do these two clips read at the resolution their metadata reports, does the finch's eye counter stay open at the card's lockup size. And the brand mark is a specific existing lockup that has to be recovered as clean vector from the team's own low resolution scan, not a fresh logo a model invents: a regenerated finch is a different mark and is not the brokerage's identity.
doability_proof: Every link sits on a surface verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), six surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. IMAGING and EXPRESS and INDESIGN and FONTS and STOCK/BOARDS are all fully headless and synchronous, and every one of the three checkpoints rests on a documented finding on those surfaces rather than on an assumption: the importer DROPS a blur filter entirely and TRUNCATES a multi layer shadow to its first layer, both at HTTP success with no warning, and the document rendition is documented as first artboard only, which is exactly why verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; the mapping readout is documented as LOSSY, dropping a run while keeping its line break so every later offset is short, with the validator returning VALID and the placeholder step returning success while mappings silently fail to land, fixed only by reconstructing the true story text from the exported document; and frame granularity from a converted PDF is documented as not under the author's control and capable of collapsing a visually separated page into a single story. PREMIERE: the RENDER and EDIT calls (media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize) are submitted through the connector and their rendered results return through the host's own progress path rather than synchronously, so this task gates NO checkpoint and NO automatic verifier on the rendered pixels of a video artifact: the cut, the grade and the mix are judged by human verifiers. It DOES gate on video_metadata, which is a synchronous headless read: probing each clip returns its true capture dimensions, which is the only thing that separates the two capture generations and the portrait pass the filenames hide, so the motion emergent checkpoint (after step 3) and its automatic verifier (A10) rest on reading metadata, of the seven sources and the delivered files' recorded dimensions, rather than on the rendered frame, and the ceiling the phone footage imposes is machine checkable without inspecting a single rendered pixel. MARK: image_vectorize is a fully headless synchronous imaging call, and recovering the Sable and Finch lockup from its only low resolution scan rests on documented behaviour, a trace that succeeds and previews clean while tracing an anti aliased halo and closing a low contrast counter, so the vector checkpoint (after step 12) rests on rendering the recovered mark at the card's real lockup size rather than on the trace's success message, and its verifier (A11) asserts vector path geometry in the mark wells rather than a re embedded raster; the vectorise strand folds onto the imaging surface, so the surface count stays six honestly counted. MERGE: one record per page for PDF is verified with page count equal to row count, per record files are producible in correct order, and 300 dpi raster requires rendering rather than merging. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, non standard numeric weights and the slug versus PostScript name trap are documented. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, a real full resolution licensed JPEG, boards persist with a hard per call placement cap and a partial success code. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no upscaling, no per artboard export, no variable QR, no bleed claim off a converted PDF, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty.
